workflow: An append-like operation accepts an iterator that reports a zero size estimate despite yielding elements.
The operation uses that estimate to retain a shared zero-terminated empty buffer with no writable element capacity.
When the first element arrives, it writes the value before checking whether the buffer must grow.
The write exceeds the shared buffer and corrupts adjacent memory, causing a buffer-overflow failure instead of safely expanding storage.
summary: Misleading zero-size estimate causes append into shared empty storage
